Everyday routines

When mornings are chaos

Make school mornings more manageable with an accessible visual routine, fewer competing instructions and practical adjustments for your autistic child.

When your child can't get started

Help your autistic child begin homework or everyday tasks with a clearer first step, appropriate support and a check for barriers that a routine cannot fix.

When bedtime takes two hours

Practical bedtime ideas for autistic children: adapt the wind-down, respond to discomfort, keep a sleep diary and recognise when medical advice is needed.

When your child won't eat

Support an autistic child with selective eating. Reduce mealtime pressure, protect accepted foods and recognise nutrition, pain or swallowing concerns.

When turning off the screen starts a meltdown

Plan screen-time transitions with your autistic child: a clear endpoint, an accessible next step and a response that protects communication and safety.

Communication and connection

When your child doesn't tell you what they need

Notice how your autistic child communicates, make requests easier to understand and explore speech, gestures, pictures and AAC without pressure to speak.

When your child keeps repeating words and phrases

Understand repeated words and phrases in autism. Notice context, respond without assumptions and find speech and language support when needed.

Overwhelm and outings

When the meltdown comes out of nowhere

Understand autistic meltdowns, reduce demands during distress and notice possible triggers. Practical parent guidance, safety considerations and further reading.

Fine at school, falls apart at home

Help your autistic child after a demanding school day. Plan a gentler arrival, compare observations with teachers and know when to seek more support.

When shops and crowds become too much

Prepare for shops and crowds with your autistic child. Consider sensory preferences, communication, breaks and an exit plan for more manageable outings.
